topology: PC1 and PC2 use separate /24 LANs on R1. R1 → R2 → R3 reaches SRV1. All three routers run classic IPv4 EIGRP100 with passive LANs and no auto-summary. Initial R1 summary lines put the desired172.16.0.0/22 on passive LAN Gi0/0 and a nonmatching172.16.4.0/22 on transit Gi0/1. Correct aggregation belongs only on transit Gi0/1. The second LAN has prepared delay30, making it the higher-metric contributor.
implemented: Sixth ENARSI Layer3 lab with independent practice/completed variants, a six-row addressing/role plan, staged guide, tested reference commands, accessible section counts and current-site domain/path/query permalinks. Existing ENARSI and39 ENCOR labs plus other categories remain available.

Initial baseline requires both remote component /24 routes and real service replies from both PCs. It proves that connectivity and configured summary lines do not establish successful aggregation. The passive LAN placement does not summarize transit advertisements; the nonmatching transit prefix has no contributors and produces no aggregate or discard.

Correct egress policy suppresses both component /24s remotely and delivers one172.16.0.0/22. Actual routes distinguish local D summary Null0 AD5/metric5120 from learned D AD90/metric7680 on R2 and10240 on R3. Three new replies in all four client/server directions prove both connected LANs still work beneath the summary.

Covered but unused172.16.2.10 requests originate on SRV1, traverse R3/R2 and are discarded at R1 Null0. Three distinct request IDs and actual router sends are correlated; TTL expiry cannot count as safe summary discard.

Narrow /24 and wrong-interface regressions require real remote component advertisements and still-successful service probes from both PCs before repair. Correct reaggregation and fresh replies from both PCs are needed after restoration.

An overbroad /16 attracts outside172.16.8.10 to R1 Null0. The repair must restore only the /22, produce three fresh outside-prefix No route drops at R3 and restore new service replies from both PCs. Merely showing a reachable valid host cannot prove the intended coverage.

With PC1 connected source withdrawn by R1 Gi0/0 shutdown, PC2 keeps the summary active. Local metric changes to10240, R2 to12800 and R3 to15360. Actual R1 discard toward PC1 and delivered replies from PC2 precede restoration and new reverse replies from both PCs.

With both contributor interfaces shut, live transit adjacencies remain but local conditional discard and both remote aggregates disappear despite the retained summary configuration. Real R3 No route drops for each PC precede restored advertisements and fresh service replies from both LANs.

HTTP success requires complete real200 responses for both PCs, each correlated with the server transaction and routed request. Thirteen tasks combine four live policy/state/save goals and nine observations. Practice starts0/13; completed reference supplies4/13 without invented packets. Earned observations survive export/import while live health and startup equality revoke on drift.

Native negative-delivery checks block reliable EIGRP UPDATE datagrams and prove remote aggregation cannot appear before actual delivery. Counterfactual tests reject fewer/unrelated probes, configuration-only toggles, PC power loss as the prescribed shutdown, static shortcuts, rewired links, changed contributor delay, broken gateways and unsaved drift.

Per-attempt epochs and normal simulator notifications capture synchronous CLI evidence with a closed guide. No simulation engine, protocol implementation, global UI, terminal styling or artwork changed.
scope: Classic IOS IPv4 EIGRP manual interface summarization. This lab has native/browser validation, not a fresh CML capture. It does not configure OSPF area ranges, BGP aggregation, IPv6, named EIGRP or leak maps. Existing ENCOR OSPF Route Summarization remains available separately.
